dedupe_keys.name: citydrain3 open source toolbox for integrated urban drainage modelling and citydrain 2

description: CityDrain3 is an open source toolbox for integrated modelling of urban drainage systems from the Unit of Environmental Engineering at the University of Innsbruck. A block library provides subsystems that together describe an integrated urban drainage system with its water and substance flows; users can use the predefined blocks or write new ones for special purposes. The page asks users to cite Burger and colleagues (2016) in Advances in Engineering Software, a paper on the design and implementation of a multicore-capable integrated urban drainage toolkit, and links the CityDrain3 project on GitHub, alongside the source code and releases of the earlier CityDrain 2 and a first version as a zip. Coverage is not tied to a place; it models any drainage system a user builds. Access is free as open source software on GitHub. Caveats: the licence name was not given on the page, GitHub could not be reached from this session to check activity, and the page gives no documentation beyond the citation. Simulation uses: coupled sewer, treatment plant and receiving water scenarios and stormwater control strategies. Related records: the Innsbruck virtual network generators (model-uibk-dynavibe-virtual-water-network-generators) and SWMM (model-epa-swmm).
